narrationScript: For our first hands-on activity, let's create a dynamic text changer. You'll build a simple web page where clicking a button changes the text and color of a heading. First, set up your `index.html` file. You'll need a basic HTML structure, an `<h1>` tag with an ID like 'myHeading', and a `<button>` with an ID like 'myButton'. Remember to link an external `script.js` file just before the closing `</body>` tag. Next, in your `script.js` file, you'll get references to both the heading and the button elements using `document.getElementById()`. Store these references in `const` variables. Now, we'll attach an event listener to your button. Use `button.addEventListener('click', function() { ... });`. Inside this function, you'll write the JavaScript logic. Set the `textContent` property of your heading variable to a new string, like 'Text has been changed by JavaScript!'. Then, also change its style by setting `heading.style.color` to 'red'. Save both files and open `index.html` in your browser. Click the button, and watch your heading transform! This exercise demonstrates the fundamental concepts of selecting DOM elements, listening for events, and dynamically updating content and styles.
